channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: TSE lança 'Pilili', mascote oficial das urnas eletrônicas no Brasil
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unveiled the mascot Pilili to celebrate 30 years of electronic voting in Brazil. The name references the sound made by the voting machine when confirming a vote. The initiative aims to make the electoral process more accessible and playful for the public.

item.title: TSE apresenta Pilili, mascote sem gênero das eleições de 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unveiled Pilili as the official mascot for the 2026 Brazilian elections, inspired by the 30-year-old electronic voting machine. Pilili is a gender-neutral character symbolizing democratic neutrality and will travel across the country to promote civic participation in voting. TSE President Minister Cármen Lúcia emphasized that the electronic voting system has eliminated fraud and ensured that each vote reflects solely the voter’s choice.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia será a relatora de ação penal contra Moro por calúnia a Gilmar
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia will be the rapporteur of the criminal action against Senator Sergio Moro for alleged slander against Justice Gilmar Mendes. The accusation stems from a video in which Moro mocked Mendes at a June party, implying he was taking bribes to grant habeas corpus. In March, the First Chamber unanimously rejected Moro’s appeal against the acceptance of the indictment.

item.title: Conselho de Ética vota suspensão de Van Hattem e mais 2 deputados
item.description: The Ethics Committee of the Chamber of Deputies is voting on Tuesday (May 5) on a report recommending a two-month suspension of the mandates of deputies Marcel Van Hattem (Novo-RS), Marcos Pollon (PL-MS), and Zé Trovão (PL-SC) for occupying the Director's Table in August 2025 during a protest against the house arrest of Jair Bolsonaro. The rapporteur, Moses Rodrigues (União Brasil-CE), argues the measure is necessary to make clear that Parliament will not tolerate conduct that obstructs the legislative process. Van Hattem labeled the process an 'endless persecution' and vowed to defend his mandate through mobilization.

item.title: Esquerda aciona MPT contra Romeu Zema por fala sobre ‘trabalho infantil’
item.description: Túlio Gadelha (PSD-PE), president of the Mixed Parliamentary Front for the Eradication of Child Labor, filed a complaint with the Labor Public Ministry (MPT) against Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate, after Zema advocated for relaxing child labor laws in Brazil. Zema’s remarks suggesting children could work under certain conditions provoked strong backlash from left-wing groups and lawmakers. The MPT will investigate potential violations of labor laws and children's rights statutes.

item.title: Associação vê propaganda eleitoral antecipada em culto de Malafaia e pede inelegibilidade de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Pastor Silas Malafaia endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential pre-candidacy during a religious service at ADVEC, interrupting liturgy to invite politicians to the altar and lead a collective prayer. The Secular Brazil Movement filed a complaint with the Rio de Janeiro Regional Electoral Prosecutor’s Office, alleging early electioneering, abuse of religious and economic power, and requesting eight years of ineligibility for Malafaia and Bolsonaro, fines, and annulment of candidacy registrations.

item.title: Líderes da oposição apostam que Alcolumbre irá barrar indicação de novo ministro do STF
item.description: Opposition leaders aim to delay the appointment of a new STF minister until after the 2026 elections, following the rejection of Jorge Messias. They acknowledge that Lula’s potential nomination of a Black female jurist with impeccable reputation would create a dilemma, as rejecting her would give the government campaign ammunition. Thus, they hope Senate President Davi Alcolumbre will block the nomination by not scheduling the hearing, taking the political heat in exchange for expected support from Flávio Bolsonaro for his Senate re-election.

item.title: Lula acerta ao lançar 'Desenrola 2.0', mas ainda não fez acenos na direção ao Centro, alertam aliados
item.description: President Lula got it right launching 'Desenrola 2.0', which relieves indebted Brazilians and supports the economy, but allies warn he is not reaching out to centrist voters. They fear his anti-system rhetoric, as in his Workers' Day speech, may alienate decisive independent voters. The strategy focuses first on reconquering his base before targeting the center.

item.title: Master: Enquanto todo mundo fala, a PF trabalha
item.description: While public discourse is dominated by narratives of conspiracy, smoke screens, and competing versions, the Federal Police continue operating silently in investigations that could shape the future of Lula’s third term. The central question is not whether political rhetoric is right or wrong, but whether PF operations will lead to real political consequences — or if this is merely another round of musical chairs. The end of Lula 3 is not yet determined, but the weight of ongoing inquiries suggests we are at a moment of decision, not spectacle.

item.title: Ida de Lula aos EUA desparafusa raciocínio de Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Lula's upcoming meeting with Trump in the U.S. surprised and confused Bolsonaro allies, particularly Eduardo Bolsonaro, who assumed the White House would prioritize his agenda. The encounter revealed that U.S. foreign policy does not revolve around bolsonarism, challenging the simplistic worldview of some opposition sectors.

item.title: As intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro entre católicos e evangélicos, segundo nova pesquisa
item.description: Lula leads among Catholic voters with 43% voting intentions, while Flávio Bolsonaro leads among evangelicals with 41%. Overall, Lula has 40% and Bolsonaro 34% in the first round, but in a potential runoff there is a technical tie with Bolsonaro slightly ahead (44% to 43%). The survey interviewed 2,000 voters between May 2 and 4, 2026, with a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

item.title: Lula, governo e PT debatem vingança por derrotas no Congresso
item.description: Lula, the government, and the Workers' Party (PT) are discussing a retaliatory response to recent legislative defeats: the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court and the overturning of the presidential veto on a law reducing penalties for crimes against the democratic regime. Growing distrust surrounds the alliance with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, and PT leaders question the wisdom of supporting Rodrigo Pacheco for Minas Gerais governor, despite Lula's endorsement. PT figures like Valter Pomar and Gleisi Hoffmann have labeled Congress as an enemy of the people, advocating for a more confrontational stance to avoid further electoral losses.

item.title: Lula orienta articuladores no Congresso a não esticar a corda com Alcolumbre, mas deve adotar postura combativa na campanha
item.description: Lula instructed his congressional articulators, José Guimarães and Randolfe Rodrigues, to avoid escalating tensions with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to prevent blocking priority agendas like the 6x1 workday and the public security PEC, despite dissatisfaction over the rejection of Jorge Messias to the STF. The strategy aims to preserve institutional relations, though government allies see the episode as an opportunity to exploit electoral themes, including evangelical support and the 'Master case'.

item.title: Lula aparece à frente de Flávio no 1º turno, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll released on May 5, 2026 shows Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round with 40% to 34%. In second-round scenarios, Lula and Flávio are technically tied (43% to 44%), while Lula defeats Renan Santos 48% to 24%. The survey also shows high rejection rates (Lula: 44%, Flávio: 41%) and 52% disapproval of Lula’s government performance.

item.title: Nem os eleitores de Lula confiam no STF, aponta Realtime
item.description: A Realtime Big Data survey released on Tuesday (5) shows that only 36% of Brazilians trust the STF, while 55% distrust the institution. Even among Lula’s (PT) voters — who appointed two current justices, Cristiano Zanin and Flávio Dino — confidence in the Court remains low, indicating a legitimacy crisis that extends to his own base.

item.title: Câmara deve votar nesta terça projeto sobre terras raras, às vésperas de reunião entre Lula e Trump
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is set to vote on Tuesday (5) on a bill establishing the National Policy for the Exploration of Critical and Strategic Minerals, focusing on rare earths. The proposal includes creating a guarantor fund of up to R$ 5 billion to encourage domestic exploration and processing, restricting raw mineral exports. The government aims to pass the bill before Lula’s meeting with Trump in Washington on Thursday (7), as Brazil holds the world’s second-largest rare earth reserves after China.

item.title: Leia detalhes da posse de Nunes Marques no TSE
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court announced the date and time for the inauguration of Minister Nunes Marques as its new president, scheduled for next Tuesday (May 12, 2026) at 7 p.m. in the plenary in Brasília. Nunes Marques, 53, was appointed to the Supreme Federal Court by Jair Bolsonaro in 2020 and has experience as an appellate judge, lawyer, and electoral judge. He succeeds Minister Cármen Lúcia after her two-year term, having been selected by seniority among STF justices serving on the TSE, with André Mendonça as vice president.

item.title: Tarifa zero no transporte poderia ser novo Bolsa Família, diz estudo
item.description: A study by UnB and UFRJ proposes that free public transport in Brazil's 27 state capitals would inject R$60.3 billion annually into the economy, with a net effect of R$45.6 billion after accounting for existing exemptions. The measure would act as an 'indirect salary' for vulnerable families, particularly Black and peripheral populations, reducing racial inequality and functioning as a new income distribution policy akin to Bolsa Família.

item.title: Novo Desenrola começa a valer nesta terça-feira
item.description: The New Desenrola Brazil program takes effect this Tuesday (May 5, 2026), offering debt renegotiation for individuals earning up to five minimum wages (R$ 8,105) with arrears between 91 and 720 days on credit cards, overdrafts, and personal loans. The initiative provides discounts of up to 90%, reduced interest rates, and the option to use FGTS to settle debts, based on Provisional Measure No. 1.355 signed by President Lula.

item.title: Educação ainda não tem a relevância eleitoral que deveria ter
item.description: Ben Schneider, MIT professor and expert on education policy in Latin America, states that education does not have the electoral relevance it should in Brazil, ranking fourth or fifth among public concerns, behind corruption and economic issues. He notes that in Chile, education became a central electoral issue in 2013 due to a broad civil society coalition and negotiations with teachers' unions, which helped pass reforms. In Brazil, he argues, the lack of such coordination between civil society, government, and unions prevents education from becoming a top electoral priority.

item.title: Durigan diz que endividamento, juros e segurança podem ampliar insatisfação com o governo Lula
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that factors such as household debt, high interest rates, and insecurity are contributing to public dissatisfaction with the Lula government, emphasizing the need to understand their root causes.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: o que são agregadores e o que podem (ou não) revelar
item.description: Election poll aggregators are tools that compile and analyze data from multiple polls to provide a more stable and representative estimate of voting intentions, reducing methodological noise. The BBC News Brasil Poll Aggregator, developed in partnership with PollingData, adjusts for differences between polling institutes, samples, and data collection periods to deliver a more reliable picture of the 2026 presidential race. Experts emphasize that while valuable for informing voters, these tools must be used with caution, transparency, and awareness of their inherent limitations.

item.title: Realtime: até Ciro Gomes empata com Lula no 2° turno
item.description: A Realtime Big Data poll released on Tuesday shows Ciro Gomes (PSDB) tied with Lula (PT) in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff, alongside Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo), all technically even with the incumbent. Flávio Bolsonaro leads with 44% voting intention against Lula.

item.title: Festa do PT tem desabafo de Jorge Viana sobre Messias, Guimarães ‘exausto’ e volta de Delúbio
item.description: At the PT's 46th anniversary fundraising dinner in Brasília, party leaders lamented the defeat in the nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, blaming the Senate and hidden interests. Jorge Viana harshly criticized Congress, calling it a 'sewer' and 'business booth', warning that the Senate battle will be decisive for 2026. José Guimarães said he was 'exhausted' due to health reasons, and the event also marked the end of the 6x1 work schedule in the menu.

item.title: PT apostava em votos de Ciro Nogueira e de 7 senadores do PL para aprovar Messias ao STF
item.description: The PT had projected 45 secure votes for Jorge Messias’s STF nomination, including Ciro Nogueira and seven PL senators, but the nomination was rejected with 42 against and only 34 in favor — the first presidential STF defeat since 1894. The PT’s political strategy was blamed for overestimating support, while government allies accused Flávio Dino and alleged a 'coup' by Moraes and Alcolumbre.

item.title: Eduardo exibe camisa que mistura Flávio e Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP) shared on X a photo alongside his brother, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), both wearing a shirt featuring the faces of Jair Bolsonaro and Eduardo himself as a 2026 presidential pre-candidate. The image was posted on May 4, 2026, during Flávio's U.S. trip, authorized by a Senate request for a political or cultural mission from May 3 to 6, coinciding with Lula's upcoming meeting with Donald Trump. The post also referenced an earlier photo by journalist Paulo Figueiredo taken at the same location.

item.title: Eleições 2026: O que muda com novas regras do TSE sobre uso de IA
item.description: Brazil's 2026 elections will be the first governed by new TSE rules on AI use, requiring mandatory labeling of synthetic content, banning deepfakes in campaigns, and imposing a 72-hour 'blackout' on new AI-generated content before voting. The measure aims to ensure transparency and protect democratic integrity amid global AI integration in politics, exemplified by cases such as a chatbot candidate in Colombia and a virtual minister in Albania.

item.title: Lula e Messias têm novo papo; permanência na AGU ganha força por enquanto
item.description: President Lula and Attorney General of the Union Jorge Messias held a new meeting on Monday (4) to discuss next steps following the Senate's rejection of Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court. Despite the congressional setback, there is growing support for the idea that Messias will remain in his current position as AGU, at least for now, with no immediate moves toward a new nomination or departure.

item.title: Quem lidera a disputa para a Presidência na eleição de 2026? Veja o agregador de pesquisas da BBC News Brasil
item.description: According to the BBC News Brasil Polling Aggregator, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leads the 2026 presidential race with 40% of voter intention in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 37% and Renan Santos at 4%. In the runoff scenario, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are in a technical tie, with 45% and 46% respectively, indicating a highly competitive election.

item.title: Dois 'apadrinhados' de Eduardo Paes estão em pé de guerra por causa das eleições
item.description: The base of Mayor Eduardo Paes is experiencing its first internal rift ahead of the 2026 elections, as federal deputy Renan Ferreira expresses irritation over the pre-candidacy of city councilman Salvino Oliveira for the Chamber of Deputies. Both are seen as Paes' protégés, but now compete for the same political space, creating tension in local political articulation.

item.title: Supremo vê erro do Executivo na derrota de Messias
item.description: Supreme Court ministers attribute Jorge Messias's Senate rejection to a political misreading by the Lula government, which underestimated congressional resistance due to its minority bloc. The third Lula term's political articulation is compared to Dilma Rousseff's, with one minister calling it 'Dilma 2 and a half', though without forecasting impeachment. The shift to mandatory parliamentary amendments since 2014 stripped the Executive of its key bargaining tool with Congress, hindering nominee approvals.

item.title: O pedido ao STF do general que tramou assassinar Lula, Alckmin e Moraes
item.description: Retired General Mario Fernandes, sentenced to 26 years and six months in prison for plotting to assassinate President Lula, Vice President Alckmin, and Justice Alexandre de Moraes, asked the STF to allow him to pay a R$ 64,800 fine in 60 installments. Despite receiving a net monthly income of R$ 23,000 as a reserve military officer, he claimed the request was necessary to preserve funds for his family’s basic maintenance. Fernandes admitted to drafting the document but described it as a 'digitized thought'.

item.title: Comissão da PEC 6 X 1 inicia trabalhos com tramitação acelerada
item.description: The special committee on the 6x1 work schedule PEC began accelerated proceedings under rapporteur Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA), aiming to reduce the weekly workweek to 36 hours over 4 days and 3 days of rest, abolishing the 6x1 shift. The rapporteur has up to three weeks to draft the proposal, with a transition period capped at five years, as the Lula government pushes for immediate effect upon promulgation, while business groups demand more time to avoid mass layoffs.

item.title: PT quer intensificar presença de Lula em podcasts e videocasts na campanha
item.description: Lula’s campaign team plans to intensify his appearances in political podcasts and videocasts during the decisive phase of the election, particularly after the party conventions in July and August. The strategy aims to reach voters through popular digital formats, reinforcing the message of his reelection bid.

item.title: Pix, minerais críticos e tarifas: o que o governo Lula quer discutir com Trump na economia
item.description: President Lula aims to discuss with Trump the review of U.S. investigations into Brazil’s Pix payment system, the removal of remaining tariffs affecting Brazilian exports, and increased investment in critical minerals. These topics, prepared by four ministries, will depend on the White House’s receptiveness ahead of the May 7 meeting.

item.title: Ação no TCU tenta driblar freio a supersalários e cria ‘teto duplex’ para servidores
item.description: An action at the TCU seeks to create a 'duplex ceiling' to circumvent the constitutional monthly salary cap of R$ 46,3 thousand for public servants, targeting trust positions in the Federal Legislature and the TCU itself through bonuses and extra-allowances. The rapporteur, Minister Walton Alencar, received R$ 592 thousand in off-cap payments in 2025, while TCU ministers collectively earned at least R$ 4.3 million in such benefits that year. Despite presidential vetoes and STF rulings against supersalaries, the practice continues via indemnities, medical reimbursements, and performance bonuses.

item.title: Congresso cria precedentes ao rejeitar indicação ao STF e manobrar regimento para não abrir CPI, avaliam técnicos
item.description: The Brazilian Congress set two unprecedented precedents by rejecting the installation of the Banco Master CPMI despite sufficient signatures and by partially overturning an integral presidential veto on the dosimetry bill. These maneuvers, led by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, bypassed long-standing rules and created new interpretations that may be repeated in future legislatures, according to legislative technicians.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0 tenta alcançar classe média: endividados terão alívio até a eleição? Analistas respondem
item.description: President Lula has launched the Desenrola 2.0 measure, expanding the debt relief program to include students, entrepreneurs, and rural farmers earning up to five minimum wages (R$ 8,105), reaching part of the middle class. The initiative aims to ease household debt burdens through 30% to 90% discounts on overdue debts (up to two years old) and allows use of up to 20% or R$ 1,000 from FGTS accounts, as part of a strategy to boost his popularity ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: BR Feminino: São Paulo vence Flamengo para assumir vice-liderança
item.description: São Paulo Women's team defeated Flamengo 2-1 to take second place in the 2026 Brazilian Women's Championship. Goals from Gabi Zanotti and Aline Milene secured the win, with Marta scoring Flamengo's consolation goal. The victory leaves São Paulo just one point behind league leaders Corinthians.

item.title: PF ainda examina contas de Lulinha três meses após autorização do STF
item.description: Three months after the STF authorized the breaking of banking secrecy, the Federal Police continues to analyze the bank accounts of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha) in search of evidence of monthly R$300,000 payments allegedly made by lobbyist Antônio Carlos Camilo Antunes (Careca do INSS). The investigation is part of the probe into INSS fraud, and while Lulinha’s defense denies involvement and awaits results calmly, investigators admit limitations in detecting cash transfers or those routed through third parties.

item.title: Bolsonaristas veem possível desgaste para Eduardo com reunião entre Lula e Trump
item.description: The upcoming meeting between Lula and Trump in the U.S. has sparked divisions within Bolsonaro's camp: some believe it could weaken Eduardo Bolsonaro due to his close ties with Trump's circle, while others see it as an opportunity for Flávio Bolsonaro to strengthen his oppositional rhetoric by highlighting perceived inconsistencies in the government's foreign policy. Although Flávio's U.S. visit was pre-planned, it is expected to be shaped by the Lula-Trump meeting, with Eduardo's allies denying any setback, while critics argue he already lost influence after the tariff controversy.

item.title: Mesmo proibidos pelo TSE, impulsionamentos de conteúdos online com ataques a adversários se tornam prática frequente do PT e do PL
item.description: Despite being prohibited by the TSE, boosting online content with attacks on adversaries has become a frequent practice for the PT and PL, using Instagram and Facebook ads to accuse Lula and Bolsonaro of crimes and spread misinformation. The PL boosted 18 publications between January and April, five of them accusing Lula of corruption and money laundering, despite those convictions being annulled by the STF. The PT, meanwhile, boosted 17 contents, seven of them attacking Flávio or Jair Bolsonaro, particularly regarding Pix and alleged ties to Trump.

item.title: Da Dona Maria ao Zé da Feira, 'fakes sintéticos' inundam as redes e driblam TSE com narrativas pró e contra governo
item.description: During the 2026 pre-election campaigns, AI-generated avatars known as 'synthfakes' have been used to spread pro- and anti-government Lula narratives on social media, exploiting loopholes in electoral legislation. These synthetic contents, more sophisticated than traditional deepfakes, hinder the TSE's efforts to combat disinformation.

item.title: Com PSD e PL liderando crescimento, um terço dos deputados estaduais do país trocou de partido durante a janela
item.description: Over one-third of Brazil's 1,059 state deputies changed parties during the 2025 partisan window, mainly benefiting the PL and PSD, which gained 34 additional seats. The PSDB saw its presence nearly halved, while small parties failed to expand. Analysts link the shift to post-2024 municipal election power dynamics and governors' influence on local politics.

item.title: Furto, roubo, estelionato e receptação: Lula sanciona lei que prevê aumento de penas no Brasil
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.397/2026, increasing penalties for theft, robbery, fraud, receiving stolen goods, and cybercrimes such as online scams and bank fraud. He vetoed a provision that would have raised the minimum sentence for robbery causing serious bodily injury above that for qualified homicide, citing disproportionality. The law also imposes stricter penalties for theft of cell phones, wires, cables, and essential infrastructure, with increased penalties for nighttime offenses.

item.title: Lula enviará novo nome ao STF antes das eleições, diz líder do PT
item.description: PT House leader Pedro Uczai said President Lula will submit a new Supreme Court nominee before the 2026 elections, following the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias — the first such rejection in 132 years. He downplayed recent government losses, including the overturning of the veto on the Dosimetry Bill, stating the Planalto will not retaliate against legislative setbacks.

item.title: Lula quer ministro 'mágico' que arranje mais dinheiro para ampliar pacote do crédito
item.description: The Lula government is seeking a minister capable of securing additional resources to expand its credit package, after the Desenrola Brasil program fell short of expectations. The debt renegotiation initiative failed to reach its target audience despite the volume of funds involved. Pressure is mounting within the governing coalition to deliver broader access to credit.

item.title: PT faz jantar de arrecadação em Brasília para celebrar 46 anos
item.description: The PT held a fundraising dinner in Brasília to celebrate its 46th anniversary, attended by party president Edinho Silva, Minister José Guimarães, and congressional leader Pedro Uczai. The event gathered around 200 participants, with tickets averaging R$1,000, and announced a collective fundraising campaign for May 15. Edinho emphasized the strategic importance of such gatherings to strengthen the party ahead of future challenges.

item.title: Governo Lula evitará vingança contra o Congresso, diz líder do PT
item.description: PT leader Pedro Uczai said the Lula government will not seek revenge against Congress after two recent defeats: the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Court and the overturning of a veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which reduces penalties for Jair Bolsonaro. Despite this, the Planoalto had considered retaliatory measures against Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The government will focus on three legislative priorities in 2026: the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule, a bill on rare earths, and reducing fuel taxes.

item.title: O novo Desenrola: até onde vai o alívio para os endividados? - O Assunto #1712
item.description: The federal government launched the new Desenrola in March 2026, allowing partial use of FGTS to pay off debts and blocking access to betting sites for participants. The program aims to reduce household debt, which reached 82.8 million Brazilians (half of all households), but economists warn that tight public finances prevent interest rate cuts, limiting relief. Analysts also note political motivation: the government seeks to regain popularity in an election year through direct-impact measures on citizens' wallets.
